paras: The New Hope posse shooting was the killing of an unnamed Black man by a bailiff named Dennis at New Hope, Georgia, on September 1, 1881, while Dennis and a posse were trying to arrest a different man. According to the wire report, the man who was shot ran out of a hut the posse had come to search and proved not to be the man they were after. Papers across the country carried the item as a short curiosity under headlines such as "Shot the Wrong Man" and "An Unlucky Negro."
A man described only as "a negro" had been charged with assaulting a woman at or near New Hope; neither he nor the woman was named in the coverage. Bailiff Dennis gathered a posse to make the arrest.

On September 1 Dennis and the posse went to a hut where they expected to find the accused man. A Black man ran out of the house, and, in most versions of the dispatch, Dennis shot and killed him. The Sacramento and Helena prints of the same dispatch say more loosely that Dennis and the posse "killed a negro who ran out." The dead man then "proved to be another man," not the one charged with the assault.
The coverage does not name the dead man or say what became of the man the posse had been seeking. No report of an inquest, an arrest of Dennis, or any other official response appears in the coverage.

The story reached print as a single telegraphic dispatch datelined New Hope, September 2, and no Georgia paper's account of it was found. The Sacramento Daily Record-Union, the Chicago Daily Tribune and the St. Paul Daily Globe ran it on September 3, the Memphis Daily Appeal on September 4, and the Helena Weekly Herald on September 8. A condensed version in a "Tragical Tales" roundup of crimes and shootings appeared in Wisconsin and Minnesota weeklies on September 7 and 10, and a Nebraska weekly summarized it as late as September 22.

Every version treated the killing as a mistake of identity rather than a crime, and none questioned the shooting itself. Headline writers stressed the error or the victim's bad luck, with titles including "The Wrong Man Killed," "Shot the Wrong Man," "An Unlucky Negro" and "Negro Killed." The roundups set the item among unrelated shootings and murders from across the country.

The Memphis Daily Appeal called Dennis "Sheriff," while every other print called him a bailiff. The St. Paul Daily Globe's version said the posse was "a party" and that the wanted man was charged with "the assassination of a woman," probably a garbling of the wire's "assaulting a woman."

reader.title: New Hope posse shooting
bases: A bailiff leading a posse to arrest an accused man shot and killed a Black man who ran from a hut and proved to be someone else (A1, A2, A5).

A man was killed (A1, A5), but by a bailiff making an arrest with a posse of unstated size (A1, A2); the papers report no seizure, no mob, and nothing beyond a shot at a man who ran, so the killing reads as an officer's shooting during an arrest, not a group killing under pretext of justice.
All prints (A1, A2, A3, A5, A6, A8, A10) derive from one New Hope wire dispatch of September 2; no independent local or follow-up account was found.
